title: One Lamp, Not Two
scene: Heavy rain on a Kent residential at morning, the kind that turns every surface into a mirror. Your left headlamp has been dying for a mile — a yellow wink, then a hole. The right is still a proper low beam. High beams would fill the rain and give you nothing but scatter, and they would give the Quiet a lighthouse. You have a spare sealed beam in the wing that takes two hands and a shoulder. You also have a running lane. The legal requirement is two lamps at night or in rain. The tactical requirement is not to stand in the street to be correct.
decision: The left lamp is dead in the rain. What do you do before the next mile?

options.text: Pull onto a driveway, shut down, swap the sealed beam, then roll on lows
options.result: You do the legal thing in the travel-adjacent. The hood is up in the rain. A volunteer comes around the curve and has to take your door line. You get the lamp on. You also spent five loud minutes being a pink island.

options.text: Hit the highs so at least one side is bright enough to count as two
options.result: The rain blooms. You cannot see past the scatter. Every window on the block has you. The dead left is still dead. You made a lighting problem into a drawing problem.

options.text: Keep rolling — one lamp is enough if you stay under twenty
options.result: A courier in dark kit cannot see your left edge. They take it as a motorcycle. Your plow teaches them otherwise at a driveway. One lamp was not a vehicle. It was a rumor.

options.text: Get off the street into a driveway well off the travel lane, then swap the beam on lows only
options.result: You take a driveway that is actually a driveway, not a shoulder. Key off. Two minutes, rain on the plating, sealed beam seated. Lows, both sides. You back out after a search. The Quiet never got a lighthouse. The next car can count you as a car.

debrief: Two working headlights in rain. High beams in rain bloom on the drops and give you nothing but scatter. Do the repair off the travel lane. A single lamp makes you look smaller than you are.

source.teaching_target: Headlights must work in pairs in rain and dark; repair off the roadway; do not use high beams in heavy rain.

image_brief.subject: the Pink Menace's front seen in a dark shop window: right low beam lit, left lamp dark, rain needles in the light
image_brief.foreground: wet glass reflection, a smear of pink plating
image_brief.midground: residential street, morning rain, no other lamps
image_brief.background: Kent houses, blinds drawn, overcast so low it is almost indoor
image_brief.read: one eye is open and one is not — that is not a legal front
